text:
Maria W: FYI — multiple orgs reporting p99 spikes starting ~11:30 PST. p95 up too. Customers see timeouts and occasional 502s. Appears concentrated in us-west2 hosted nodes. Repro: curl against /v1/generate, model=redwood-2.0-quant, seq=1024, batch size normal. Posting logs and quick repro steps below.

OncallBot: ALERT: latency_tail_usw2 · p99 increased from 410ms -> 1.9s at 2026-03-15T18:28:40Z. Incident ID: LAT-20260315-01. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/latency/LAT-20260315-01

Samir: I see the same in traces — large spikes in service inference time, not the HTTP layer. Traces show long kernel time on GPU host 10.12.5.14. There was a runtime rollout at 18:28UTC that touched kernel selector + quantized path. Correlation looks strong.

Devon: Can we immediately route traffic off the rolled runtime or fallback to redwood-2.0-quant-lite? Also suggest putting a circuit-breaker at 1s for the public route until we narrow root cause.

Ashley: Customer "acme-corp" already opened an escalation. They asked for ETA. Please be explicit about mitigation so I can update CS. :pray:

Kevin: Collecting quick evidence before any rollback. Autoscaler events show queue_length spike and batching grew to ~512 tokens/batch for long sequences. Possibly batching policy + a kernel scheduling regression = long-per-batch latency.

Maria W: Repro snippet I used:
```bash
# rapid repro (do not run in prod)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.0-quant","input":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Trace snippet (shortened):
```
span: inference_kernel_exec (GPU 0) duration=1.6s
span: batch_schedule wait=120ms
span: kv_cache fetch=14ms
```

Samir: Quick checks I ran: cpus/pinning looks fine. Kernel logs from host show a busy loop inside int8 attention path starting at 18:28:37. Patch was deployed then: runtime v2.3.7 -> v2.3.8. I recommend either rollback runtime or route to model variant that uses different execution path.

Devon: Proposed immediate mitigations (short checklist):
1) Add temporary rate-limit for noisy customers (per-API-key) to 20 req/min or 1 req/s sustained.
2) Put a circuit-breaker at the gateway: fail fast if backend >1s or error rate >2% for 1m windows.
3) Route traffic from us-west2 to us-west1 fallback region for affected customers.
4) Pin critical customers to redwood-2.0-quant-v2 (prior build) or redwood-2.0-quant-lite.
5) Reduce max_batch_size in serving config to 64 to avoid huge batches.
6) Enable KV prefix cache for chat flows to reduce decode tokens.

Kevin: I'm ready to roll back runtime on the canary pool if we get sign-off. Rollback steps: `deployctl rollback --target runtime --version v2.3.7 --pool canary-usw2` (will take ~3–5m to converge). If rollback doesn't help, we switch routing.

Maria W: Ashley — tell customer we're doing mitigations now: temporary rate-limits + circuit-breaker and will either rollback runtime or route them to fallback model. ETA ~15–30m.

Ashley: Sending update to acme-corp with that ETA. They're asking for the playbook so they can understand how retries/backoff should be implemented client-side.

Devon: I'll apply a temporary gateway circuit-breaker rule and reduce max_batch_size on live serving config. Commands: 
```
# gateway rule (example)
PUT /gateway/rules/circuit-breaker
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "latency_ms": 1000, "consecutive_failures": 5, "action": "open" }
```
And runtime config: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/inference-serving MAX_BATCH_SIZE=64
```

OncallBot: Action queued: circuit-breaker-rule-1761234567 applied by Devon at 18:35:12Z.

Samir: After CB + reduced batching (18:36UTC) we're seeing p99 drop from 1.9s -> 430ms on the affected pool. p95 back to ~200ms. Still monitoring.

Kevin: Rolling back canary runtime now to v2.3.7 on the small pool (commands issued). Will watch host-level metrics.

Maria W: I pushed a routing flag to move 15% of production traffic to redwood-2.0-quant-lite as a gradual fallback.

OncallBot: Metric update: p99_usw2 = 390ms at 18:42:01Z. Error rate normalized.

Ashley: Customer acknowledged update: "Thanks, the tail latency improved — we'll watch and will disable our aggressive retries for now." :thumbsup:

Devon: Follow-ups to add to runbook (please PR into runbooks/latency-playbook.md):
- Immediate detection: dashboard thresholds for p95/p99, correlate with deployments.
- Fast mitigations: gateway CB, per-key rate-limits, and routing to fallback model/region.
- Medium mitigations: reduce batching, enable prefix KV cache, restrict long-sequence offerings temporarily.
- Rollback/Release: criteria for rollback vs. routing. Include exact commands and expected customer-visible impact.
- Post-incident: postmortem owners, timeline, and regression test for kernel selector.

Kevin: I'll open a PR for rollback procedure and include the `deployctl` commands + validation checklist. Samir, can you capture the kernel logs and file a bug against runtime v2.3.8 with attached traces?

Samir: On it. Captured GPU kernel stack traces and will file a detailed issue with perf diffs.

Maria W: Closing loop: current status — mitigations applied (CB, reduced batching, partial routing). p99 back to baseline in us-west2. Will keep this thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks all.

Ashley: Customer follow-up scheduled in 1h. I'll include the playbook actions and next steps.

Devon: Action items assigned: Kevin (rollback PR + runbook updates), Samir (bug + logs), Devon (CB rule & runbook section), Maria (customer comms + ops timeline).

OncallBot: LAT-20260315-01 updated: status=mitigated, mitigations=[circuit_breaker, reduced_batching, fallback_routing], incident_owner=Maria W.

Kevin: Quick note — if we add these mitigations to the SLO guardrails: recommended thresholds: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for standard model; circuit-breaker open at backend latency >1000ms; per-key QPS caps default 5 rps, burst 10. Add as defaults in console.

Maria W: Adding that to the runbook notes. Will follow up with a short postmortem draft tomorrow.

Ashley: Thanks everyone. I'll ping when customer is fully satisfied. :heart:
